simple.meaning: כַּרְבֵּל (karbêl) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to gird or clothe.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in 1 Chronicles, beginning at 1 Chronicles 15:27. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to כַּרְבֵּל (H3736) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: כַּרְבֵּל (karbêl) / H3736 is traced through 1 Chronicles 15:27 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H3736. karbel [ כרבל ] verb either denominative be-mantle (from Biblical Aramaic כַּרְבְּלָא Dan 3:21 , if this = mantle , and not (Marti Gl. ) = Assyrian karballatu , cap (but 'Kriegs[?]-Mantel,' Zehnpf BAS ii, 535 )), or possibly quadril. bind round (from כבל , with insert ר ); — only Pu`al Passive participle בּוּץ בִּמְעִיל מְכֻרְבָּל 1Chr 15:27 bemantled with a robe of byssus.
